response.sql:
WITH kept AS (
  SELECT driverId, points, wins
  FROM driverStandings
  WHERE points > 1.0
),
per_driver AS (
  SELECT driverId, AVG(points) AS avg_points, AVG(wins) AS avg_wins
  FROM kept
  GROUP BY driverId
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_avg_wins FROM per_driver
)
SELECT p.driverId, p.avg_points, p.avg_wins, p.avg_wins - o.mean_avg_wins AS wins_diff
FROM per_driver p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.mean_avg_wins IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY wins_diff IS NULL, wins_diff DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The higher side of the 1.0 dividing line means points strictly greater than 1.0, so records with exactly 1.0 are dropped.
Averages are taken over the kept records only, with NULL points or wins ignored by AVG; a driver with no kept records is absent from the result.
The 'proceed only if the mean exists' condition is implemented as returning zero rows when the overall mean of per-driver average wins is NULL.

alternatives.interpretation: The higher side includes the dividing line itself, so records with points equal to 1.0 are kept (points at or above 1.0).
